title: Trilobatin rescues cognitive impairment of Alzheimer's disease by targeting HMGB1 through mediating SIRT3/SOD2 signaling pathway.
authors: Gao, Jian-Mei; Zhang, Xun; Shu, Guo-Tao; Chen, Na-Na; Zhang, Jian-Yong; Xu, Fan; Li, Fei; Liu, Yuan-Gui; Wei, Yu; He, Yu-Qi; Shi, Jing-Shan; Gong, Qi-Hai
one_liner_zh: 该文研究三叶苷通过HMGB1/SIRT3/SOD2通路改善阿尔茨海默病认知障碍，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with cognitive impairment that currently is uncurable. Previous study shows that trilobatin (TLB), a naturally occurring food additive, exerts neuroprotective effect in experimental models of AD. In the present study we investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying the beneficial effect of TLB on experimental models of AD in vivo and in vitro. APP/PS1 transgenic mice were administered TLB (4, 8 mg. kg(-1) .d(-1), i.g.) for 3 months; rats were subjected to ICV injection of Abeta(25-35), followed by administration of TLB (2.5, 5, 10 mg. kg(-1) .d(-1), i.g.) for 14 days. We showed that TLB administration significantly and dose-dependently ameliorated the cognitive deficits in the two AD animal models, assessed in open field test, novel object recognition test, Y-maze test and Morris water maze test. Furthermore, TLB administration dose-dependently inhibited microglia and astrocyte activation in the hippocampus of APP/PS1 transgenic mice accompanied by decreased expression of high-mobility group box 1 (HMGB1), TLR4 and NF-kappaB. In Abeta(25-25)-treated BV2 cells, TLB (12.5-50 muM) concentration-dependently increased the cell viability through inhibiting HMGB1/TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. HMGB1 overexpression abrogated the beneficial effects of TLB on BV2 cells after Abeta(25-35) insults. Molecular docking and surface plasmon resonance assay revealed that TLB directly bound to HMGB1 with a K(D) value of 8.541x10(-4) M. Furthermore, we demonstrated that TLB inhibited Abeta(25-35)-induced acetylation of HMGB1 through activating SIRT3/SOD2 signaling pathway, thereby restoring redox homeostasis and suppressing neuroinflammation. These results, for the first time, unravel a new property of TLB: rescuing cognitive impairment of AD via targeting HMGB1 and activating SIRT3/SOD2 signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）是一种进行性神经退行性疾病，伴有认知障碍，目前无法治愈。既往研究表明，三叶苷（trilobatin, TLB）作为一种天然食品添加剂，在AD实验模型中发挥神经保护作用。在本研究中，我们探讨了TLB在体内和体外AD实验模型中发挥有益作用的分子机制。APP/PS1转基因小鼠接受TLB（4, 8 mg·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹，灌胃）治疗3个月；大鼠接受脑室内注射Aβ(25-35)，随后给予TLB（2.5, 5, 10 mg·kg⁻¹·d⁻¹，灌胃）治疗14天。我们显示，TLB给药显著且剂量依赖性地改善了两种AD动物模型中的认知缺陷，通过开放场测试、新物体识别测试、Y迷宫测试和Morris水迷宫测试评估。此外，TLB给药剂量依赖性地抑制了APP/PS1转基因小鼠海马中小胶质细胞和星形胶质细胞的激活，并伴随高迁移率族蛋白B1（HMGB1）、TLR4和NF-κB表达降低。在Aβ(25-35)处理的BV2细胞中，TLB（12.5-50 μM）通过抑制HMGB1/TLR4/NF-κB信号通路浓度依赖性地增加细胞活力。HMGB1过表达消除了TLB在Aβ(25-35)损伤后对BV2细胞的有益作用。分子对接和表面等离子体共振实验显示，TLB直接结合HMGB1，K(D)值为8.541×10⁻⁴ M。此外，我们证明TLB通过激活SIRT3/SOD2信号通路抑制Aβ(25-35)诱导的HMGB1乙酰化，从而恢复氧化还原稳态并抑制神经炎症。这些结果首次揭示了TLB的新特性：通过靶向HMGB1并激活SIRT3/SOD2信号通路来挽救AD的认知障碍。
